summary: Console widget ghost series after org-attribute sync and org-switch
description:
Issue summary:
Users at NovaApps opened reports that a dashboard widget (heatmap/time-series) surfaces metric series that do not correspond to any recent requests — we’re calling this a 'ghost' series. The ghosted series appears immediately after an organization-attribute synchronization job (org-attribute-sync) and when end-users switch context between orgs in the console.

Impact:
- Affected dashboards show duplicated or persistent series that misrepresent usage and can trigger false alerts.
- Customer reports billing and SLA concerns because displayed per-org usage spikes are not attributable to any API keys.
- Occurs intermittently (~1–2% of org-switch events for this customer) but reproducible.

Observed first occurrence: 2026-03-09 18:42 UTC (customer report).

Why this is customer-facing support: dashboards are the source of truth for cost and SLO monitoring for NovaApps' platform team; inaccurate series lead to operational confusion and potential billing disputes.
steps_to_reproduce: Use NovaApps account (dedicated) in prod us-east
Open console -> Dashboards -> select org-scoped heatmap for 'token_count' metric
Have org-attribute-sync job run (runs at 18:40 UTC by default) or trigger manual org sync
Switch org context in console back-and-forth 2–3 times
Observe an extra series appear in the heatmap that persists past several minutes and is not linked to any API key in the usage export
logs: usage-rollup svc returned join records where org_id_map contained both old and new attributes: trace_id=7f9c, window=2026-03-09T18:40:00Z
query-cache (console) served a pre-sync cached result for dashboard tile id=tile_9b2f with etag mismatch
console tracehook log: TRACEHOOK-20260309-1843: widget_render served_series_count=6 but backend query returned 5 unique series
customer-provided sample request id: req_0a1b2c showing no activity at the spike timestamp
comments: 2026-03-10 | Aisha Patel: Customer reported persistent duplicate series after org sync; attached screenshot and CSV export from NovaApps.

2026-03-10 | Diego Ramos: Acknowledged; assigned to me for triage. Initial hypothesis: org-attribute-sync job updates org metadata but usage-rollup joins on stale attribute keys cached in query-cache.

2026-03-11 | SRE (Megan Chen): Confirmed race window in rollout logs. Found that org-attribute-sync writes to org-attrs table then emits kafka event; downstream usage-rollup consumes per-window but console query-cache TTL is 5m — possible stale join key. Collecting JVM GC and consumer lag metrics.

2026-03-12 | Support (Aisha Patel): Provided workaround to customer: manual dashboard refresh and forced cache invalidation via console -> Settings -> Invalidate Widget Cache. Customer validated that ghost series disappeared after cache invalidation.
2026-03-12 | Diego Ramos: Preparing a mitigation: add immediate cache-invalidate trigger on org-attribute-sync events for affected orgs; working with infra to test in staging.
investigation_notes: Reproduced in staging with synthetic org-switch after org-attribute-sync job; console served a cached tile with stale 'org_tag' join key for ~2m.

usage-rollup commit window alignment: rollup aggregates run on 1m windows; if org-sync updates attribute between rollup aggregation and console cache write, joins can include both old and new attribute rows (duplicate time-series).
Kafka consumer lag observed spike up to 12s during customer's repro window — may exacerbate mismatch but not necessary for ghosting to occur.

Hypothesis: combination of (1) eventual consistency between org-attrs table and usage-rollup materialized view, and (2) console query-cache TTL + ETag mismatch leads to tile rehydration containing both legacy and new join keys.
next_steps: Backfill acceptance tests in staging that simulate org-attribute-sync + org-switch + dashboard read within 0–3 minutes
Implement immediate cache invalidation on org-attribute-sync events for affected orgs (short-term mitigation)
Add an integration test that asserts dashboard tiles do not return duplicate series after attribute changes
Long-term: consider making usage-rollup join on stable org IDs only and normalize org attribute change window with transactional hooks or outbox pattern
resolution: Mitigation in progress: implemented a staged patch that triggers per-org widget cache invalidation when org-attribute-sync publishes change events. Patch landed in redwood/console PR 4127 and staged to qa on 2026-03-12. Customer workaround (manual cache invalidation) validated the symptom disappearance. Next: monitor customer for 48h and push hotfix to prod after QA sign-off.
